stem:
Navya lists everyday uses on a chart: oxygen for breathing, nitrogen in fertilisers for plants, and chlorine to purify drinking water. Metal pans and wires sit on the same table.

Which claims correctly judge the importance of non-metals? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Non-metals such as oxygen, nitrogen, and chlorine are essential in everyday life alongside metals.
Nitrogen is used to purify drinking water.
Chlorine helps purify drinking water, so non-metals matter even when metals are visible as pans and wires.
Only the metal pans and wires matter in everyday life.

teacher.key_rationale: Oxygen, nitrogen, and chlorine have essential everyday uses, so non-metals matter even when metal tools are visible. Nitrogen is not the water-purifying non-metal here; chlorine is. Visible metals alone do not make non-metals unimportant.
